chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin al-Darir from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no riba (usury/interest) between a man and his son, nor between him and his slave, nor between him and his family; rather, riba is only between you and what you do not own.
I asked: So are the polytheists riba between me and them? He said: Yes.

I said: For they are your slaves. He said: Indeed, you do not own them; you own them along with others, you and others are equal regarding them. And what is between you and them is not of that [category], because your slave is not like your slave and the slave of another.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of riba in relation to family and slaves according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between riba in familial/domestic spheres and riba in commercial/external transactions, asserting that relationships with one's own dependents do not incur riba because of direct ownership. He clarifies that while polytheists (or non-Muslim subjects) are considered 'owned' in a broader sense, the transactional dynamic with them differs from that with one's own slaves, as the latter involves exclusive dominion whereas the former involves shared or comparative ownership among the community. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that riba is primarily a defect in exchange contracts between independent parties rather than a structural feature of hierarchical domestic relations.
